key_insight: A genome-guided, physics-informed ML pipeline can screen vast lead-free double perovskite space and identify phase-stable absorbers using interpretable descriptor families tied to structure and optoelectronic behavior.
engineering_relevance: This provides practical design rules for discovering non-toxic, all-inorganic semiconductor candidates for photovoltaics, sensors, and transparent electronics with DFT-validated stability.
method: Train ML surrogates on 1,221 DFT-calculated A2BB'X6 compounds using packing, bonding, polarization, and electronic-identity descriptors.
Use a staged inverse-design constraint stack to filter 13,088 charge-balanced lead-free compositions.
Validate top candidates with DFT and convex-hull stability checks.
evidence_signal: The stability classifier achieved ROC-AUC 0.92, the band-gap regressor reached R2 = 0.93 on held-out data, and five final candidates were DFT-validated on the convex hull.
watch_item: The workflow is strong for screening, but practical deployment still depends on experimental synthesis, defect tolerance, and real-device stability beyond DFT thermodynamics.
paper_title: Genome-Guided Interpretable Screening of Phase-Stable, Lead-Free Double Perovskite Absorbers for All-Inorganic Semiconductors, Sensors, and Photovoltaics with DFT-Validated Design Rules
